speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry with the new plans for increased reliance on low-carbon hydrogen fuel to address our power needs (a) what sources will the hydrogen come from; (b) how will the Government prepare our infrastructure to transport and store hydrogen; (c) whether the potential increase in spending on infrastructure will lead to significant cost increases for consumers; and (d) how will the Government work with regional countries to encourage the take-up and production rate of hydrogen for energy use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: A growing pipeline of production projects from around the world is being announced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Key technologies that enable the transportation and use of hydrogen in various carrier forms, such as ammonia, are also expected to become commercially ready in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The projects will also allow us to co-create solutions with the industry and develop rules and regulations to enable hydrogen supply chains in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To enable widespread deployment of hydrogen in Singapore, new infrastructure, or the retrofitting of existing infrastructure, will be required.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Such infrastructure will likely include import terminals that can unload hydrogen, large storage facilities and a distribution network to get the hydrogen to its end-use sites.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In developing the long-term infrastructure development roadmap, we will need to strike a careful balance between the pace of roll out to enable decarbonisation and the cost.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To that end, we will take into consideration a range of factors, including the pace of technological and supply chain development of low-carbon hydrogen and the relative attractiveness of hydrogen vis-à-vis other low-carbon alternatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will also identify synergies for hydrogen adoption across different sectors and applications, to create greater economies of scale and to derive savings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Besides domestic infrastructure, we also need to establish regional and global low-carbon hydrogen supply chains, so that we can import the hydrogen we need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Singapore adopts a diversified portfolio in importing our energy to ensure security and resilience, and we will take the same approach for hydrogen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Where we import from and in what quantities will depend on a few factors, such as the availability of exports, costs and the need for diversification in sources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We are working closely with our international partners to enable these supply chains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Singapore has signed several MOUs with countries that have made significant strides in their hydrogen efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Together, we will collaborate on areas, such as advancing interoperable and mutually recognised guarantees of origin certifications for low-carbon hydrogen, facilitating the physical movement of hydrogen across the borders and joint R&D efforts to overcome technological challenges.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Can MTI now share more on how this can be achieved and what is Singapore's target for the adoption of low-carbon hydrogen?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: How much hydrogen is Singapore expected to import in 2050?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: And to meet this net-zero goal by 2050, how soon and how fast can we expect to scale up hydrogen adoption, especially green hydrogen?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member, Dr Lim Wee Kiak, for his supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Hydrogen will form an important part of our nation's long-term, low-emission development strategy and effort to fight climate change – a topic that we spent four hours talking about and debating during yesterday's Sitting.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: However, like I shared earlier, there still remain some uncertainties in two areas, the technological development as well as the supply chain.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Supply chain development is critical because it involves transportation and storage.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And we will do so by embarking on smaller-scale projects.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As we do so, we want to co-create the solutions with the industry.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And as we do so, we want to develop rules and regulations to enable that hydrogen supply chain in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As we embark on all these small-scale projects, this will allow us to scale up our workers, as well as the industries and also the Public Service officers in the Government to build up our capabilities in this important area.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In developing our long-term infrastructure development plan for hydrogen, we are very mindful to keep our eyes and ears on the developments globally on what is the emerging technology in this area that is cost-effective and safe, and to strike a very careful balance between the speed of the rollout and the cost.
